question.text: Which of the following statements about the Basic Savings Bank Deposit Account (BSBDA) is CORRECT in the context of PAN requirements?

answer.text: Opening a BSBDA does not require submission of a PAN card
BSBDA opening requires a PAN card just like any other savings bank account
BSBDA requires both PAN and full KYC but allows a 6-month grace period for document submission
BSBDA is governed by SEBI rather than RBI and is exempt from PAN requirements on that basis

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook lists the Basic Savings Bank Deposit Account (BSBDA) among the categories where a PAN card is not required for opening the account. KYC norms generally apply to bank accounts, but the specific source-backed point being tested here is the PAN-relaxation for BSBDA. The Trap: Candidates may treat BSBDA exactly like a standard savings account and assume PAN is mandatory, or they may attribute the relaxation to SEBI versus RBI jurisdiction. Neither is correct on the checked pages — the PAN exemption for BSBDA stands on its own. Note: Source basis is pp.297-298 of the NISM-Series-X-A Investment Adviser (Level 1) workbook (June 2025), which lists BSBDA among accounts that can be opened without PAN.
